goal: No lane hits a platform limit: the shared operator key never bursts into 429s.

hypothesis: The apps' limiter is a 60/min sliding window that does not count refusals. 653 of 1,121 requests were 429s because each client retried on its own fixed 5 s timer (agent-ask ignored Retry-After) instead of sharing the key's allowance.

baseline.value: 1,121 requests, 653 x 429 on the shared operator key (2026-10-10)

prediction: On a harness of 8 concurrent lanes against a 60/min key, the current tools produce a 429 burst; the budgeted tools produce 0 429s and finish in a comparable wall time.
falsifier: The budgeted harness shows any 429 burst, or finishes much slower than the key's limit allows.

goal: Any fix in any Tangle agent-app repo reaches production in under 30 minutes; gates survive host loss.
lever: beelink-gate: auto host choice, launcher-death watchdog over the stdin heartbeat, one hold budget per gate, lock fd not inherited, holder metadata and dead-holder reclaim, receipts.jsonl, --ship (exact scripts/ship.sh verify), runs from either beelink without GTR
hypothesis: Locks were held for 72 minutes because a killed GTR launcher left the beelink's bash and vitest running: nothing on the remote side read stdin, and the command inherited the lock. Waits piled up because each lane named one beelink. GTR going offline (23:39Z on 2026-10-10) stopped every gate because the entry point and the chains lived only there.

baseline.value: lock wait up to 72 min on beelink1; no wait or hold receipts; GTR is the only launcher host in the docs

prediction: A killed launcher frees its lock within 60 s and leaves no remote processes. A hung command stops at the hold limit (default 45 min). auto starts on the free beelink, so receipts.jsonl shows no wait over 10 min while either beelink is free. Gates run from the Mac or either beelink while GTR is down.
falsifier: A live-proof case fails, or receipts.jsonl shows a wait over 10 min while the other beelink was free.

goal: Gates survive host loss and pick a host that can start now.
lever: beelink-gate: policy read falls back from reg.exe to SSH to the cached last good read; probe reports free host slots and auto ranks hosts with a slot first
hypothesis: Launched from beelink1, auto marked beelink1 unreachable because WSL interop failed (UtilAcceptVsock accept4 failed 110), and chose beelink2 whose four host slots were full, so the gate queued.

baseline.value: self probe unreachable from beelink1; auto queued on a full host (4 slots running)

prediction: From either beelink, auto sees both hosts and starts on the one with a free slot.

result.harness: 8 concurrent agent-ask status lanes, 12 turn reads each, fake operator API with a 60/min sliding window and Retry-After, beelink2

outcome: 0 x 429 and 41% fewer requests. Wall time 1.7x on a saturated burst, because the default host share (50/min) keeps 10/min headroom under the key's 60. The prediction of comparable wall time is falsified for a burst; OPERATOR_API_RATE_PER_MIN=60 gives a single host the full limit.
learnings: A refusal-free budget costs throughput only when the key is saturated; the headroom is the price of sharing one key across hosts.
